newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Wharf's New T&T expands HK fixed network.
newsitem.headline: Wharf's New T&T expands HK fixed network.

text.p: Wharf (Holdings) Ltd's telecommunications arm, New T&T Hong Kong Ltd, has extended the reach of its fixed telephone network by installing exchange equipment in a Hong Kong Telephone Company exchange near the Central business district.
"We negotiated a deal with Hong Kong Telephone Company to allow us to locate our exchange equipment in their exchanges," said New T&T president Leslie Harris in an interview on Wednesday.

"That means that in effect almost any customer in a Hong Kong Telephone exchange where we are co-located has the potential to be a New T&T customer without us having to dig up roads and pull wires into buildings," Harris added.
The company is one of three to benefit from the government's decision to end Hong Kong Telephone Company Ltd's monopoly on domestic telecommunications services in Hong Kong in June 1995.
Hong Kong Telephone is a 100-percent subsidiary of Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd.
Harris said New T&T currently is concentrating on serving Hong Kong's commercial sector customers, chiefly in Central.
"We are concentrating on the golden bowl," said Harris.
The company will instal its equipment in an exchange on the eastern tip of Hong Kong island next week.
The company did not disclose the terms of its agreement with Hong Kong Telephone.
New T&T will be permitted to locate its own equipment in all Hong Kong Telephone Company's exchanges after negotiating commercial terms with Hong Kong Telephone.

"The interconnection agreement between the new telephone service providers and Hong Kong Telephone Company is only a temporary measure," Harris said. "New T&T will continue to build its own fixed line network."
The company in its first year of operations connected 10,000 subscribers and had 150,000 international call subscribers, said Harris.
It will have connected 78 buildings, mainly in the Central business district, making them available to its network by the beginning of 1997, he added.

New T&T, along with Hutchison Telephone Co Ltd, 70 percent held by Hutchison Whampoa Ltd and New World Telephone, a subsidiary of New World Development Ltd, were awarded licences to develop domestic fixed line telecommunications services when the Hong Kong Telephone monopoly ended in mid-1995.
